title: STree: Speculative Tree Decoding for Hybrid State-Space Models
venue: arXiv 2505.14969 (NeurIPS 2025 per search listing, not seen on abs page)
quote: We propose the first scalable algorithm to perform tree-based speculative decoding in state-space models
proves: Prior SSM spec decode could not do tree verification; STree uses accumulated state-transition-matrix structure to verify a token tree on pure SSM and hybrid models with little overhead.
does_not_prove: Abstract gives no speedup numbers; baseline drafter and simple tree only; no serving-system integration, batching, or memory accounting across many requests.
bearing: Supports hybrid tree-verification ideas; threatens any candidate claiming hybrid tree verify is unaddressed

title: Bole: Efficient Tree Speculation for Hybrid-Attention Language Models
quote: reducing transient state memory by 82--99×
proves: Tree-structured closed form for linear-attention recurrence; reconstruct only the selected state; 82-99x less transient state memory, 3.4-7.7x faster linear-attn tree verify, up to 4.72x offline decode throughput, 2.03x over best tree baseline.
does_not_prove: Offline throughput; says nothing about preemption, prefix-cache checkpoints, migration of speculative state, or online scheduling.
bearing: Threatens kernel-level hybrid rollback candidates; leaves serving-state lifecycle open

title: TreeWY: Speculative Verification for Gated DeltaNet Hybrids
quote: snapshot the full recurrent state at every draft position for GDN layers
proves: Current systems snapshot full GDN state per draft position and snapshots cannot be shared across tree branches; TreeWY stores a small pseudo-value matrix and reconstructs only the accepted state, cutting speculative state memory and KV pressure at identical acceptance length (Qwen3.5 35B/397B).
does_not_prove: Abstract: wider tree enabled by freed memory is not yet a throughput win; gains only where memory binds, a few percent cost otherwise; no numbers in abstract.
bearing: Second independent hybrid-tree kernel in Aug 2026; kernel space crowded; memory-capacity-to-admission angle less covered

title: [Model][Spec Decode] Nemotron-H MTP and Mamba Speculative Decoding Support (vLLM PR 33726)
quote: the following features are confirmed to cause bugs and/or crashes when used with speculative decoding and mamba2: - Chunked Prefill - Prefix Caching
proves: vLLM Mamba2 spec decode (merged Feb 2026) separates prefill/decode state indices and uses num_accepted_tokens to select SSM state slots; chunked prefill and old-style prefix caching broke, and async scheduling is ineffective because state update forces a sync.
does_not_prove: Feb 2026 state; later PRs may have fixed some gaps; no perf numbers.
bearing: Supports candidates on hybrid spec decode x scheduling/prefix caching interaction

title: [Perf][Hybrid] Reserve Mamba speculative-decoding scratch per running request instead of per KV-concurrency slot (vLLM PR 57261)
quote: that 9 was being multiplied by 19.4 concurrency slots although only 8 requests can ever speculate at once
proves: vLLM charges each hybrid request num_speculative_blocks extra Mamba state pages per group; on GLM-5.3-Flash MTP k=3, 9 of 45 blocks per request are speculative scratch, reserved per KV-concurrency slot rather than per running request.
does_not_prove: PR was CLOSED unmerged; only reported capacity changes, not allocation; no throughput data.
bearing: Supports memory-accounting/admission candidate: speculative recurrent scratch is mis-budgeted

title: [Perf][Spec Decode] Defer GDN spec decode state stores to the next step (vLLM PR 61434)
quote: For Qwen3.8-27B that is 3 MB per sequence per layer per token, and most of those states are thrown away.
proves: GDN spec verify writes full fp32 state after every draft token (3 MB/seq/layer/token); kernel was 18% of GPU time at concurrency 64; deferring stores and replaying accepted tokens gives +5.6% (c16) and +10.6% (c64) throughput with DFlash k=7, no change at c1.
does_not_prove: Open PR, one run per point, MI355X only; requires fp32 state and prefix caching off (align mode keeps old path).
bearing: Shows per-draft state write cost scales with batch; overlaps rollback-by-replay ideas

title: [Spec Decode][Qwen4Exp] RecoverSSM for Qwen GDN and the PLE short conv (vLLM PR 58863)
quote: Speculative decoding on Gated DeltaNet today snapshots the full recurrent state after every draft position, and reserves one Mamba block per draft position.
proves: vLLM already has a RecoverSSM verify/commit protocol (Kimi-K3 KDA) that keeps num_speculative_blocks=0 by storing small per-token replay records; extending it to GDN enlarges pages ~6%, which widens hybrid prefix-cache block alignment (1,600 to 1,664 tokens) and can lose a block of prefix reuse; K=2 c=1 measured 1.9-4% slower.
does_not_prove: Open PR; competing ReplaySSM ring-buffer PRs exist; no scheduling or preemption analysis.
bearing: Threatens 'replay instead of snapshot' as novel; reveals coupling of spec state layout to prefix-cache granularity

title: [Core] Default prefix_cache_retention_interval to dense for Mamba + EAGLE (vLLM PR 55760)
quote: leaving Mamba checkpoints largely unreachable — prefix caching never hits for the Mamba cache group
proves: With sparse Mamba checkpoint retention, EAGLE dropping the tail block from prefix hits made Mamba prefix caching hit 0 tokens; fix reverts to dense checkpoints for Mamba+EAGLE.
does_not_prove: Fix is a default change; cost of dense checkpoints (memory) not quantified; other retention PRs open.
bearing: Strong support for spec-decode x hybrid prefix-cache checkpoint placement as a live systems problem

title: [Performance]: MTP first repeat misses prefix cache on a hybrid Mamba/GDN model (vLLM issue 53504)
quote: with MTP speculative decoding the **first repeat of an identical prompt misses the prefix cache entirely and re-prefills in full**
proves: Production-style trace: Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 hybrid, MTP k=2, 12k-token prompt repeated serially; first repeat re-prefills fully with spec on, hits immediately with spec off; EAGLE-adjusted reusable boundary differs from retained Mamba checkpoint.
does_not_prove: Single model/config; issue closed after workaround; TTFT cost across workloads not measured.
bearing: Supports multi-turn/agentic prefix reuse x spec decode on hybrids candidate

title: [Bugfix] Fix GDN conv + SSM state corruption with ngram spec decode (vLLM PR 40738)
quote: After a spec decode step accepts N tokens, the next non-spec decode step must read SSM state from block N-1 and conv state from an offset position.
proves: Rollback for hybrids has two pieces of state (SSM and conv window) and alternating spec/non-spec steps corrupted output with ngram on Qwen3.5 GDN.
does_not_prove: Correctness bug, open PR; no perf data.
bearing: Shows correctness fragility of hybrid rollback when speculation is intermittent (ngram may not draft every step)

title: n-gram speculative decoding for hybrid GDN targets (vllm-metal PR 1072)
quote: A partial acceptance currently re-scans all requests in the batch, including any prefill rows.
proves: On Apple Silicon (M5 Max, Qwen3.8-27B 4-bit, batch 1): ngram on hybrid GDN gives 2.22x on 30K repeated text but 0.71x on 30K diverse and 0.95x on 8K diverse; drafts capped at state-block boundaries to keep align-mode checkpoints exact; rollback is a re-scan of accepted prefixes.
does_not_prove: Single-stream only, measured before a correctness follow-up; greedy only, sync scheduling only; ngram only.
bearing: Directly on user hardware: rollback-by-rescan cost and batch-wide rescan are open; supports Metal-side hybrid rollback candidate

title: Support built-in MTP draft head speculative decoding with prefix caching on hybrid GDN models (vllm-metal issue 610)
quote: draft-state rollback across mamba state blocks (num_speculative_blocks) is not implemented. Disable one of the two.
proves: As of Aug 2026 (still open), vllm-metal refuses MTP spec decode together with prefix caching on hybrid GDN models.
does_not_prove: PR 1072 later added ngram only; native MTP + prefix caching still missing as of issue state.
bearing: Opportunity on user's stack: MTP + hybrid prefix-cache rollback on Metal

title: Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context
quote: typically runs full attention over the entire KV cache
proves: MTP draft heads use full attention even on hybrid/linear targets, so draft KV read dominates at long context; sliding window on the draft only cuts per-step draft cost 28-44% at 1M context and drops ~99% of draft KV; unread draft KV is 7.7-11% of total KV.
does_not_prove: Single-GPU, 1M context; single author; does not study batching or eviction policy for draft KV.
bearing: Supports draft-KV memory hierarchy / eviction candidates on hybrid targets; threatens naive draft-KV windowing as novel

title: vLLM Now Supports Qwen3-Next: Hybrid Architecture with Extreme Efficiency
quote: Better memory management, plus the support of automatic prefix caching and P/D disaggregation for hybrid models.
proves: Sept 2025: vLLM supported Qwen3-Next MTP via a hybrid KV cache manager; prefix caching and P/D for hybrids were roadmap items.
does_not_prove: Dated baseline; later PRs (F5-F9) show partial delivery.
bearing: Context for timeline of hybrid spec decode support

title: Utility-Driven Speculative Decoding for Mixture-of-Experts
quote: speculation causes slowdowns up to 1.5x, making it infeasible
proves: Draft tokens collectively activate more experts, raising data movement and verification time 2-3x; spec decode can slow MoE serving up to 1.5x; Cascade limits slowdown to 5% and gains 7-14% over static K.
does_not_prove: No hybrid/recurrent models; does not tie expert union to batch size or KV pressure jointly.
bearing: Supports speculation-length control for MoE; threatens simple 'adaptive K for MoE' as novel

title: MoE-Spec: Expert Budgeting for Efficient Speculative Decoding
quote: enforcing a fixed expert capacity limit at each layer
proves: Training-free per-layer expert cap during verification gives 10-30% higher throughput than EAGLE-3 at comparable quality.
does_not_prove: Lossy (drops tail experts); quality tradeoff; no offload/edge setting.
bearing: Threatens expert-budget verification ideas

title: Less Experts, Faster Decoding: Cost-Aware Speculative Decoding for Mixture-of-Experts
quote: selecting draft tokens also determines the union of experts activated during verification
proves: Expert scattering: high-probability draft tokens route to disjoint experts; EcoSpec puts expert cost into draft-tree selection, up to 1.62x on DeepSeek-V3.1, Qwen3-235B-A22B, GPT-OSS-120B.
does_not_prove: No per-request batching interplay across many requests stated in abstract.
bearing: Threatens cost-aware MoE draft-tree candidates

title: S2-MoE: Enabling Efficient Self-Speculative Decoding for Mixture-of-Experts on Edge Devices
quote: naively combining them often incurs excessive verification overhead and poor expert reuse
proves: Edge MoE self-spec in llama.cpp with routing-aware expansion and reuse-aware gating: up to 5.3x, about 2.0x average over AR.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not detail expert offload or unified memory bandwidth.
bearing: Threatens edge MoE spec decode candidates; check device class vs Apple Silicon

title: SpecReason: Fast and Accurate Inference-Time Compute via Speculative Reasoning
quote: their combination yields an additional 8.8-58.0% latency reduction
proves: Small model speculates whole reasoning steps, base model judges; 1.4-3.0x over vanilla LRM inference; stacks with token-level spec decode for 8.8-58.0% more latency reduction.
does_not_prove: Lossy (semantic acceptance); does not address KV/state of rejected steps or serving with batching.
bearing: Step-level speculation adds rejected-step KV as new state; serving-side handling open

title: Scaling Speculative Decoding with Lookahead Reasoning
quote: Lookahead Reasoning improves the speedup of SD from 1.4x to 2.1x while preserving answer quality
proves: Token-level SD on reasoning has an algorithmic ceiling; step-level drafts expanded in one batched pass compound with token SD (1.4x to 2.1x).
does_not_prove: Multiple parallel step branches multiply KV state; no serving memory/scheduling study.
bearing: Supports branch-KV management candidates for step speculation

title: Beat the long tail: Distribution-Aware Speculative Decoding for RL Training
quote: reduces rollout time up to 50% while preserving identical training curves
proves: RL rollouts: suffix-tree drafter built incrementally from recent rollouts plus larger draft budget for long trajectories; up to 50% rollout time reduction.
does_not_prove: Suffix tree memory and staleness across policy updates not quantified in abstract.
bearing: Threatens suffix-tree-for-RL candidates; suffix tree as cross-request state is established

title: Taming the Long-Tail: Efficient Reasoning RL Training with Adaptive Drafter
quote: TLT achieves over 1.7x end-to-end RL training speedup over state-of-the-art systems
proves: Draft model trained continuously on idle GPUs during long-tail rollout keeps alignment with drifting policy; >1.7x end-to-end.
does_not_prove: Datacenter multi-GPU setting; not applicable to single laptop.
bearing: Threatens RL rollout drafter-staleness candidates

title: Fast LLM Post-training via Decoupled and Fastest-of-N Speculation
quote: SpecActor is 1.1--2.6x faster compared to vanilla speculative rollout in different traces
proves: Decoupled and fastest-of-N speculation for RL rollout: 2.0-2.4x mean rollout speedup, 1.4-2.3x end-to-end training.
does_not_prove: Large-batch GPU clusters only.
bearing: Crowded RL-rollout spec area; low opportunity for a laptop-scale thesis

title: SuffixDecoding: Extreme Speculative Decoding for Emerging AI Applications
venue: arXiv 2411.04975 (NeurIPS 2025 Spotlight per abs page comments)
quote: agentic frameworks typically submit repetitive inference requests
proves: Suffix trees over prompts and prior outputs give up to 5.3x on SWE-Bench and Text-to-SQL agent workloads, 2.8x over EAGLE-2/3.
does_not_prove: Suffix tree memory growth, eviction, and persistence across restarts not addressed in abstract.
bearing: Suffix tree as serving state (caching/eviction/checkpoint) remains a systems lens

title: AgentSpec: Speculative Decoding for Batch Inference of LLM Agents
quote: state-of-the-art speculative decoding algorithms exhibit substantial speed degradation under large batch sizes
proves: Agent batch inference: high rejection rates and unused dynamic token budgets degrade spec decode at large batch; structure-isolated drafting plus redundancy-aware budget allocation, evaluated in vLLM.
does_not_prove: No speedup numbers in abstract; no hybrid models.
bearing: Threatens agent-workload verification-budget candidates

title: AgSpec: Pushing the Limits of Retrieval-Based Speculative Decoding in Coding Agent Pipelines
quote: ignore that accept length varies across agents and drifts over turns
proves: Coding-agent retrieval drafting; acceptance drifts over turns and across agents; per-agent online draft caps give up to 4.37x (batch 1) and 4.76x (batch 16).
does_not_prove: Oct 2026, very recent; corpus memory cost and cross-session persistence not described in abstract.
bearing: Threatens per-agent adaptive draft length; supports corpus/state lifecycle questions

title: Speculative Actions: A Lossless Framework for Faster Agentic Systems
quote: Across domains, we achieve up to 55% next-action prediction accuracy, translating into up to 20% latency reductions.
proves: Action-level speculation for agents: up to 55% next-action accuracy, up to 20% latency reduction.
does_not_prove: Above the token level; does not touch KV or serving state.
bearing: Low bearing on token-level serving state; adjacent work

title: Streaming Tokens and Tools: Multi-Turn Agentic Harness Support in Dynamo
quote: Some models intentionally drop prior thinking on ordinary assistant turns.
proves: Reasoning parsers decide whether earlier-turn thinking is kept, transformed, or dropped, which changes the prefix and causes prefix-cache misses; varying header raised TTFT 168 ms to 912 ms on a 52K prompt.
does_not_prove: Does not mention speculative decoding; reuse of dropped thinking traces as draft material is not discussed.
bearing: Supports 'reasoning trace reuse across turns as draft source' candidate (no source found doing it)

title: DFlash: Block Diffusion for Flash Speculative Decoding
quote: over 6x lossless acceleration across a range of models and tasks
proves: Block diffusion drafter conditioned on target hidden features drafts a block in one forward pass; >6x lossless, up to 2.5x over EAGLE-3.
does_not_prove: Abstract silent on draft-side state (target features buffer) under batching/preemption, and on hybrid targets.
bearing: Large fixed blocks (k=7-16) amplify per-draft recurrent-state cost on hybrids (see F6)

title: MagicDec: Breaking the Latency-Throughput Tradeoff for Long Context Generation with Speculative Decoding
quote: We leverage draft model with sparse KV cache to address the KV bottleneck
proves: Sparse-KV drafter makes spec decode pay off at batch 32-256 for long sequences; up to 2.51x for Llama3.1-8B.
does_not_prove: Dense-attention targets; pre-hybrid; no preemption analysis.
bearing: Threatens sparse-KV-draft candidates; establishes large-batch long-context regime

title: QuantSpec: Self-Speculative Decoding with Hierarchical Quantized KV Cache
quote: employs a hierarchical 4-bit quantized KV cache and 4-bit quantized weights for acceleration
proves: Self-spec with hierarchical 4-bit KV and weights; >90% acceptance, up to ~2.5x, ~1.3x less memory than sparse-KV self-spec.
does_not_prove: Long-context single-request focus; no multi-tenant memory pressure study.
bearing: Threatens KV-compressed draft candidates

title: Lossless but Not Free: An Empirical Anatomy of Speculative Decoding on Consumer Hardware
quote: speculative decoding pays off only when verification is genuinely batch-parallel and the draft/target latency gap is real.
proves: On an Apple-silicon laptop, 3 of 5 draft/target backend configurations got slower; quantized Metal backend executes parallel verification serially; best 1.61x at K=6 with acceptance falling 69.7% to 37.8%.
does_not_prove: No bandwidth measurements in abstract; single laptop; batch 1.
bearing: Strong negative result for user hardware; supports measuring verify parallelism on Metal before anything else

title: Cross-Family Speculative Decoding for Polish Language Models on Apple Silicon: An Empirical Evaluation of Bielik 11B with UAG-Extended MLX-LM
quote: verification cost on unified memory does not amortize as theory predicts because both models are memory-bandwidth bound
proves: On Apple Silicon with MLX-LM, draft and target both bandwidth-bound on shared memory; 1.7x on structured text, no speedup on varied instructions.
does_not_prove: Single model pair, batch 1, language-specific.
bearing: Negative result for separate-draft spec decode on unified memory; favors model-free or MTP drafters

title: MemSpec: Memory-Aware Runtime for Adaptive Draft Scheduling in Speculative Decoding on Edge Devices
quote: decouples draft selection from execution through proactive resident working-set management
proves: Edge (Jetson Orin Nano): multiple drafts under tight memory; mismatch between draft selection and draft availability; proactive resident-set management +40.7% steady-state throughput over bandit adaptive methods.
does_not_prove: Jetson, not Apple Silicon; draft weights residency only, not KV/recurrent state.
bearing: Threatens draft-residency scheduling candidates on edge

title: [Mamba] Speculative Decoding Mamba (vLLM PR 37985)
quote: hybrid models have layers in multiple KV cache groups - attention layers share one group while mamba layers have their own
proves: Separate-draft-model spec decode for Jamba/Mamba1 hybrids needed multi-group KV handling in the proposer; tested Jamba2-Mini + Jamba2-3B with low acceptance.
does_not_prove: Closed unmerged; no numbers.
bearing: Separate draft models on hybrids remain poorly supported; MTP/ngram dominate

title: Vegas / SpecAttn: Self-Speculative Decoding with Verification-Guided Sparse Attention
proves: Search snippet: sparse-attention self-spec reusing verification-time KV criticality; up to 2.81x over AR.
does_not_prove: Not opened.
bearing: Threatens sparse-attention self-spec candidates

title: SparseSpec (PillarAttn)
proves: Search snippet: self-spec with PillarAttn, unified scheduler, delayed verification, KV offload; up to 2.13x throughput for reasoning.
does_not_prove: Not opened.
bearing: Threatens sparse-self-spec-with-scheduler candidates

title: BubbleSpec: Turning Long-Tail Bubbles into Speculative Rollout Drafts for Synchronous Reinforcement Learning
proves: Search snippet: model-free RL rollout spec targeting first epoch where prior-epoch reuse gives nothing.
